rows.question: Why are the dot products scaled by the square root of d_k?
rows.answer: The dot-product between a query and a key grows proportionally to the dimension \(d_k\); as \(d_k\) becomes large the raw dot products become very large in magnitude, which drives the softmax into regions with extremely small gradients. Dividing (scaling) the dot products by \(\sqrt{d_k}\) keeps their scale moderate, stabilising the softmax and preserving useful gradients [p.4].
